title: A clinical trial to learn more about the effects of VAY736 in people with Sjögren's disease
official: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-arm multicenter Phase III study to assess the efficacy and safety of ianalumab in participants with Sjogren's disease with high symptom burden (THALASSA)
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate superiority of ianalumab over placebo based on the change from baseline in the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) oral dryness score at Week 52
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Male or female participants ≥ 18 years of age or as per country-specific legal adult age,  whichever is higher
2. Classification of Sjögren's disease according to ACR/EULAR 2016 criteria.
3. Seropositive for anti-Ro/SSA antibodies at screening
4. SSSD oral dryness score ≥ 5 and overall SSSD summary score ≥5 collected over 14 consecutive days during the Screening 2 period
5. Screening ESSDAI biologic and/or hematologic domain > 0 ;  Note: laboratory abnormalities for scoring must be confirmed as associated with Sjögren's disease and not be due to other underlying conditions.  • If during screening visit cryoglobulins are being assessed locally as part of standard  clinical practice they can be included in the ESSDAI scoring, but patients may be  enrolled without screening results of cryoglobulins, provided all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met  • There is no upper limit on the screening ESSDAI score; however, the percentage of  participants with ESSDAI ≥ 5 will be restricted to no more than 15% of the population.
6. Stimulated whole salivary flow (sSF) rate > 0.3 mL/min at Screening
7. Participants taking hydroxychloroquine (≤ 400 mg/day) are allowed to continue their  medication, and must have been on a stable dose for at least 4 weeks prior to screening, which should be maintained throughout the 52 weeks of the blinded treatment period.
8. Predniso(lo)ne ≤ 5 mg/day or equivalent are allowed for up to 16 weeks post-  randomization.  • Participants taking systemic corticosteroids have to be on a stable dose of ≤ 5 mg/day predniso(lo)ne or equivalent for at least 4 weeks prior to screening.  • Tapering of background corticosteroids must be performed, starting at randomization, with dose tapering to 2.5 mg or less predniso(lo)ne (or equivalent) over the course of 16 weeks maximum, with a goal of tapering to 0 mg/day of steroid if possible
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presence of another autoimmune rheumatic disease that is active and constitutes the  principal illness, specifically:  • Moderate-to-severe active systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) with anti-dsDNA  positivity and renal involvement, or other organ involvement  • Active rheumatoid arthritis (RA)  • Systemic sclerosis (SSc)  • Any other associated connective tissue disease (e.g., lupus nephritis (LN), large vessel vasculitis (LVV), Sharp syndrome (mixed connective tissue disease)) that is active  and requires immunosuppressive treatment outside the scope of this trial and would  impede on Sjögren's disease organ domain assessments.
2. Concurrent diagnosis or history of fibromyalgia or overlapping inflammatory diseases
3. Prior treatment with a B-cell-depleting therapy (e.g., rituximab, other anti-CD20 mAb, anti- CD22 mAb, or anti-CD52 mAb) within:  • 36 weeks prior to randomization, or  • As long as B-cell count is less than the lower limit of normal (LLN) or baseline value prior to receipt of previous B-cell-depleting therapy (whichever is lower) at  Screening.
4. Prior treatment with ianalumab
5. Prior treatment with any of the following within the given period prior to Screening:  • Within 5 half-lives prior to Screening: iscalimab (anti-CD 40 mAb), belimumab (anti-BAFF mAb), abatacept (CTLA4-Fc Ig), anti-tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFα) biologic agents, immunoglobulins (i.v./s.c.), plasmapheresis, or any other investigational biologic medicines under investigation for Sjögren's disease  • Within 4 weeks OR drug-specific 5 half-lives elimination period (if longer than 4  weeks) prior to screening: i.v. or oral cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate mofetil  (MMF), methotrexate, azathioprine, i.v. or oral cyclosporine A or any other  immunosuppressants (e.g., JAK inhibitors or other kinase inhibitors).
6. History of hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs or their excipients, or to drugs of  similar chemical classes (e.g., mAb of IgG1 class) or to any of the constituents of the  study drug formulation (sucrose, L-histidine hydrochloride/L-histidine, polysorbate 20).
